record.paper_title: Retrieving Convex Bodies from Restricted Covariogram Functions
record.context_brief: Baire-generic origin covariogram data in higher dimensions
record.original_question: In d-dimensional Euclidean space with d >= 3, consider convex bodies K and H and the covariograms g_K and g_H. Say GC({o}) holds when g_K(x) = g_H(x) for all x in some neighborhood of the origin o. In the Baire category sense, where a property holds for most convex bodies if the exceptions form at most a meager set and a meager set is a countable union of nowhere dense sets, is it true that for most convex bodies K, every convex body H satisfying GC({o}) must coincide with K up to translations and point reflections?

evidence.quote: GC(X) The equality gK(x) = gH(x) holds for all x in some neighbourhood of X.

Thus, we may speak about statements that hold for most convex bodies, i.e., for all convex bodies with at most a meager set of exceptions. We recall that a set is said to be meager if it is a countable union of nowhere dense sets and residual if it is a complement of a meager set.
Theorem 6. In the Baire category sense, for most convex bodies K and all convex bodies H in E d the following statements hold true.
II. If d = 2 and K and H satisfy GC({o}), then K and H coincide, up to translations and reflections.
It is an open question whether Part II of the statement can be carried over to convex bodies of higher dimensions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 3$ and let $\mathcal{K}^d$ denote the space of convex bodies (compact convex sets with nonempty interior) in $\mathbb{R}^d$, endowed with the Hausdorff metric (which makes $\mathcal{K}^d$ a complete metric space, so Baire category applies). For a convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, the covariogram of $K$ is the function
$$g_K(x)=\mathrm{vol}_d\bigl(K\cap(K+x)\bigr),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^d.$$
For two convex bodies $K,H\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, say that the condition $\mathrm{GC}(\{o\})$ holds if there exists an open neighborhood $U$ of the origin $o\in\mathbb{R}^d$ such that $g_K(x)=g_H(x)$ for every $x\in U$.

A subset of $\mathcal{K}^d$ is meager if it is a countable union of nowhere dense sets; a property is said to hold for most convex bodies if the set of bodies failing it is meager.

Question: Is it true that for most $K\in\mathcal{K}^d$, every convex body $H\in\mathcal{K}^d$ such that $K$ and $H$ satisfy $\mathrm{GC}(\{o\})$ must coincide with $K$ up to translations and point reflections (i.e., $H=\pm K+t$ for some $t\in\mathbb{R}^d$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The Baire-generic determination of convex bodies by their covariogram in higher dimensions is known. Goodey, Schneider and Weil established that most (in the Baire sense) convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge 3$, are determined up to translation and point reflection by the covariogram, and this has been extended to the restricted setting where only the covariogram near the origin is prescribed, as part of Theorem 6 in the work treating restricted covariogram data.

status_evidence.title: The covariogram problem (survey, Bianchi)
status_evidence.snippet: Most convex bodies in R^m are uniquely determined (up to translation and reflection) by their covariogram; for m>=3 the result has been proved by Goodey, Schneider and Weil.
status_evidence.claim: Generic determination by the covariogram is established in all dimensions d>=3.

status_evidence.title: Retrieving convex bodies from restricted covariogram functions
status_evidence.snippet: Most convex bodies are determined, within all convex bodies, by their covariogram in any arbitrarily small neighborhood of the origin.
status_evidence.claim: The restricted (neighborhood-of-origin) Baire-generic determination is proved.
